extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners subject to USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) proceedings; OED staff and USPTO officials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state-court attorney discipline, including service, notice, duties of an excluded practitioner, publication, and reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the exclusion of a respondent from practice before the USPTO may be ordered for violation of ethical standards (here: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may impose exclusion identical to discipline imposed by a state court in reciprocal disciplinary proceedings. The Final Order states exclusion is appropriate where the respondent was disbarred on ethical grounds by a state court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order to respondent (mailing to last known address)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order is mailed by certified mail to the respondent at the last address known to the OED Director (example: certified mail with receipt number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing to the last known address is the primary method of service; the Notice informs the respondent of the Complaint and the opportunity to respond within the regulatory period. The example shows certified-mail service and tracks delivery attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication under 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b) when unable to serve
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office is unable to serve the respondent at the last known address, the respondent may be served by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b) in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication must include information that the OED Director initiated the proceeding and instructions on how to request copies of the Notice, Order, and supporting documents; example publication dates are provided (e.g., Nov. 22 and Nov. 29, 2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's time to respond and permissible grounds to oppose under § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not file a response within the 40-day period, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and find reciprocal discipline appropriate. The 40-day period begins from the mailing/publication as specified in the Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard and basis for imposing reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by a state court (reciprocal discipline) pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59, based on a state order disciplining the attorney for ethical violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state-court findings (e.g., disbarment for neglecting client matters, misrepresentation, settling without client consultation, failing to cooperate with Bar Counsel, and violations of specific state Rules of Professional Conduct) serve as the factual and legal basis for the USPTO's reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion and public posting of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is directed to publish a formal 'NOTICE OF EXCLUSION' in the Official Gazette describing the respondent, the fact of exclusion, and the reasons for discipline; disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should identify the respondent, state the regulatory basis for the exclusion (citations given), summarize the state-court findings, and provide the OED Reading Room link (http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) for public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is or formerly was admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inter-agency/court notice requirement serves to communicate the USPTO's reciprocal disciplinary action to other jurisdictional authorities and the public as required by § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of an excluded practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner is directed to comply with duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties applicable to excluded practitioners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically directs the respondent to comply with § 11.58 and to submit proof of compliance with specified subsections when seeking reinstatement; although the text does not list § 11.58's full contents, it requires compliance as a condition of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition and proof requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the respondent must submit proof of compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(b)(3), (b)(5), and (b)(6) to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order makes reinstatement contingent on demonstrating compliance with the specified duties of an excluded practitioner; petitioners should review § 11.60 and the cited § 11.58 subsections to ensure required proofs are supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of exclusion (date of Final Order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusion from practice before the USPTO is effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states the exclusion becomes effective on the issuance date of the Final Order; practitioners should treat the exclusion as immediate upon entry.
